Young Thug, born Jeffery Lamar Williams, is an influential American rapper, singer, and songwriter from Atlanta, Georgia, widely recognized as one of the defining figures of 2010s hip-hop and trap music. He broke into the mainstream consciousness in 2014 with hits like “Stoner” and “Danny Glover” before building a massive critical following with projects like *Barter 6* and the *Slime Season* mixtape series. He quickly stood out in the genre for his unconventional vocal style—switching rapidly between high-pitched squeaks, melodious crooning, and rapid-fire flows—as well as his fluid approach to fashion.

—

Beyond his own multi-platinum discography, including chart-topping albums like *So Much Fun* and major features such as Camila Cabello’s hit “Havana,” he launched the record label YSL (Young Stoner Life), serving as a mentor to prominent artists like Gunna and Lil Baby. His career hit a major crossroads in May 2022 when he was arrested in Atlanta under a sweeping state RICO indictment alleging gang activity. Following one of the longest criminal trials in Georgia state history, he resolved the charges in October 2024 by entering a non-negotiated plea deal, allowing him to be released from custody on strict probation conditions.
